pack.title: Science & Nature
pack.description: Stars, storms, creatures, elements and the words scientists borrowed.

categories.title: PLANETS
categories.triviaFact: Saturn is the least dense planet, with an average density lower than that of water.

categories.title: PRECIPITATION
categories.triviaFact: Hailstones grow in layers as updrafts carry them repeatedly through freezing parts of a storm cloud.

categories.title: ROMAN GODS
categories.triviaFact: Vulcan, the Roman god of the forge, gives his name to the word volcano.

categories.title: ___FLY
categories.triviaFact: A firefly's glow comes from bioluminescence, a chemical reaction that gives off almost no heat.

redHerrings.note: MARS and VENUS are Roman gods as well as planets, but JUNO, MINERVA, VULCAN and DIANA already complete the gods, so all four planets stay together.

categories.title: FLOWERS
categories.triviaFact: Tulip bulbs became so valuable in the 1630s Dutch Republic that the episode is called tulip mania.

categories.title: INSECTS
categories.triviaFact: Male crickets chirp by rubbing a scraper on one wing against a toothed ridge on the other.

categories.title: FOUND IN A FLOWER
categories.triviaFact: Sepals are the small leaf-like parts that protect a flower bud before it opens.

categories.title: ___ BEE
categories.triviaFact: Spelling bees borrow an old sense of bee meaning a gathering of people working together.

redHerrings.note: QUEEN and WORKER describe ant castes too, tempting you toward the insects, but BEETLE, ANT, WASP and CRICKET are complete; both pair with BEE.

categories.title: NOBLE GASES
categories.triviaFact: Helium was detected in the Sun's light in 1868, decades before it was found on Earth.

categories.title: EVERYDAY METALS
categories.triviaFact: Cobalt takes its name from kobold, a mischievous goblin of German mining folklore.

categories.title: MONEY NAMES
categories.triviaFact: The rupee takes its name from the Sanskrit rupya, a word associated with wrought silver.

categories.title: ELEMENTS NAMED AFTER PLACES
categories.triviaFact: Marie Curie named polonium after Poland, her homeland, which was not then an independent state.

redHerrings.note: A NICKEL is a US coin, but PENNY, DIME, PESO and RUPEE already make four money names, so NICKEL stays with the metals.
COPPER's name traces back to Cyprus, yet it is not one of the elements named after modern places; it is an everyday metal.

categories.title: CLOUD TYPES
categories.triviaFact: Cirrus clouds form so high in the sky that they are made almost entirely of ice crystals.

categories.title: NAMED WINDS
categories.triviaFact: The mistral is a cold northerly wind that funnels down the Rhone valley to the Mediterranean.

categories.title: WEATHER INSTRUMENTS
categories.triviaFact: Evangelista Torricelli built the first mercury barometer in the 1640s.

categories.title: HIDDEN WEATHER
categories.triviaFact: Thailand was known to outsiders as Siam until the country officially changed its name in 1939.

redHerrings.note: MISTRAL hides MIST just like MISTAKE, but it is needed with SIROCCO, CHINOOK and BORA as a named wind.
RAIN GAUGE openly contains rain, but it is an instrument; the hidden weather words conceal it inside other words.

categories.title: WILD CATS
categories.triviaFact: A cheetah can sprint at around 100 kilometers per hour, but only for short bursts.

categories.title: MARSUPIALS
categories.triviaFact: Wombats are famous for producing cube-shaped droppings, a rarity in the animal kingdom.

categories.title: COLLECTIVE NOUNS FOR ANIMALS
categories.triviaFact: A group of whales or dolphins is called a pod, and some orca pods stay together for life.

categories.title: ___ BEAR
categories.triviaFact: The teddy bear is named after US President Theodore Roosevelt, who refused to shoot a captive bear.

redHerrings.note: People often say koala bear, but a KOALA is a marsupial, not a bear; POLAR, TEDDY, GUMMY and GRIZZLY complete that group.
PRIDE points at lions and the wild cats, but it is a word for a group of animals, not a cat.

categories.title: AUSTRALIAN CITIES
categories.triviaFact: Darwin, capital of Australia's Northern Territory, is named after the naturalist Charles Darwin.

categories.title: SI UNITS
categories.triviaFact: One watt equals one joule of energy transferred every second.

categories.title: PARTS OF AN ATOM
categories.triviaFact: Protons and neutrons are built from smaller particles called quarks, held together by gluons.

categories.title: SCIENCE ___
categories.triviaFact: The term science fiction was popularized in 1929 by the magazine editor Hugo Gernsback.

redHerrings.note: DARWIN and NEWTON look like a pair of famous scientists, but NEWTON is a unit of force and DARWIN is a city in the Northern Territory.

categories.title: ENGINE TYPES
categories.triviaFact: Rudolf Diesel demonstrated his compression-ignition engine in the 1890s, and it still bears his name.

categories.title: DRAWING TOOLS
categories.triviaFact: A protractor measures angles and is usually marked from zero to 180 degrees on a half circle.

categories.title: FOUR GREAT INVENTIONS OF CHINA
categories.triviaFact: The oldest known dated printed book is the Diamond Sutra, printed in China in the year 868.

categories.title: ___PAPER
categories.triviaFact: Flypaper is coated with a sticky substance that traps insects as soon as they land on it.

redHerrings.note: A COMPASS also draws circles, but RULER, PROTRACTOR, PENCIL and STENCIL complete the drawing tools; the magnetic compass is a great Chinese invention.
PAPER sits right next to the ___PAPER group, but the word itself cannot be completed that way; it is one of the Chinese inventions.

categories.title: BURROWING ANIMALS
categories.triviaFact: Armadillo means little armored one in Spanish, after the bony plates covering its back.

categories.title: CHEMICAL BOND TYPES
categories.triviaFact: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules help explain why water has an unusually high boiling point.

categories.title: WORDS FOR A SPY
categories.triviaFact: A sleeper is an agent placed in a foreign country who stays inactive until called upon.

categories.title: ___ CELL
categories.triviaFact: Solar cells convert sunlight directly into electricity using semiconductor materials such as silicon.

redHerrings.note: A MOLE is the classic burrowing animal, but RABBIT, MEERKAT, GOPHER and ARMADILLO fill that group; here MOLE is a spy.
PLANT cell and SLEEPER cell both sound right, but FUEL, STEM, SOLAR and PRISON complete the cells, and the spies need both words.
